title: Apple TV 4K Wi-Fi 64GB (3rd Gen) $265 + $7.42 Shipping @ Retravision
body:
Deal: Apple TV 4K Wi-Fi 64GB (3rd Gen) $265 + $7.42 Shipping @ Retravision

[kbd67] I just got the 128gb model for 230 in this august
[koplik88] I've still got the very first one in the cupboard. They stopped updates so it's completely useless. New thought to buy another one
[YawningTrooper58] These last for an decade before you will need an upgrade. I know the price is high but kinda worth it in the long run.
[babyyodathethird] Genuinely curious, what is the point of an apple tv? Like most tvs nowadays are 'smart' especially if all you need to do is watch netflix or prime, etc is there any difference?
[get-innocuous] Just faster, no ads and a good chance the streaming apps will be better than what your tv offers (Kayo in particular seems basically non functional on a lot of TVs but works perfectly on an Apple TV).
[FrugalSplack] @get-innocuous: Kayo is 100% fine on Google TV Streamer - have personally tested it
[bataleon] Clean interface and no ads is what sold me. I hated seeing ads on my LG and Sony home screen from services I didn't even subscribe to.
[SavvyBeans] I’ve been kind of tempted recently. My lounge room TV has become laggy, this would let me keep the big screen without upgrading the TV completely. I also AirPlay my iPhone to the TV to share family videos with everyone, but there’s always been a slight audio lag. This would fix that too
[lisalt] @SavvyBeans: Yeah that’s what I’ve always done over the years. Get the cheapest high quality panel (TCL), shove an Apple TV on it and boom. Was gonna hold out until Black Friday but not looking promising on price and old stock with the new release. Second hand stock (market place and eBay) is fleeting and asking prices are comparable
[Fuzor] They're meant to go into a console replacement category but every year Apple doesn't do enough with gaming so if you already have a post 2019/2020 tv then you wouldnt need it
[team teri] I was told privacy is better. Sure, the streaming service will always know what you watch, but if you use Google TV, they keep track of everything in addition, same with Fire TV and Amazon. Less tracking with Apple TV.
[jmys01] Just to add to this, along with the Apple TV being faster, having better app support, not bombarding you with tacky and irritating advertising, and giving you the option of AirPlay if you have other Apple devices, another major plus for the Apple TV is also much better privacy.
Some people might not care about this, but plenty certainly do, including me. Smart TVs spy on everything you do and sell that information on to data brokers and advertisers. I personally find this very creepy and don't want to be subjected to it. My 'smart' TV has never been connected to the internet. I just use it as a screen and use the Apple TV for all the smart features. While it's certainly not perfect, it's a lot better from a privacy perspective.
[vlahka] Like others said, the streaming apps work better on this than on tvs. They sometimes have little framerate skips. Plus I've noticed quality during streaming sometimes fluctuates if you pay real close attention. The apple tv is supreme. If you use plex this is even better because theres an app called 'Infuse' that links with plex and lets you play media through that instead. This app handles high bitrate videos and HDR/DV much better than plex. Even plays some files plex has trouble with. Its only an extra $20 a year subscription but I've found I couldnt live without it after the annoyances of plex on its own and other players from vlc to kodi etc.
[FrugalSplack] They’re not worth it though because Google TV Streamer can be had for $80 or less on sale and has all the same apps and features.
And I say that as a heavy Apple user. Apple TV is one of their worst products. Even before the price hikes it was way too expensive. Paying $265 for one of these four year old boxes is absurd, unless you desperately need some niche Apple feature you can’t get on the other products or just directly through your smart TV.
[get-innocuous] Google tv is full of ads and is slow as hell though
[FrugalSplack] @get-innocuous: I really don’t have that experience with the Streamer. If anything it’s often more zippy than the Apple TV, and faster to open apps. And for one third the price.
Just saying one is “full of ads” and one isn’t, isn’t a very helpful or accurate comparison. Yes I’d say the Google has more ads (although this can be reduced), but Apple does have ads (Apple TV app has ads, full screen “content previews” are on by default for your main apps, and of course, the actual apps you’ll be using like Netflix and YouTube are all full of ads by default).
And again, one third the price. Yes the Apple is better, but unless you just don’t care about money at all, it’s extremely hard to argue it’s 3x better than the Google. The Google is like 95% as good imo and in some ways better.
[Tommybot] $195 a year ago for the 128gb model. And I distinctly recall feeling ripped off. Better off buying second-hand at this price.
[FlipperMeTimbers] be glad, its $449 now for the fourth gen. absolute rip off. i bought a preowned 2nd gen 4k for $99, does literally everything the exact same
[HunterBargainHunter] I almost got it for $178 but thought it’s long in the tooth already and better wait for the next gen.
Well, next gen is here, and it’s standing behind a figurative AI sodomiser that wants its share of the action.
[kumquat] Better off getting Google TV streamer, can at least sideload and put on a launcher to get rid of ads, ad free YouTube, stremio, kodi
[hawktalk] I've been interested in the past but no usb slots = no buy from me. My priority is watching content off a hdd vs streaming.
If I get desperate for streaming apps I can use a google chromecast (eg amazon prime tv works better on that, vs the prime app on the tv itself).
[lisalt] Can run a plex server locally, and download the plex app on Apple TV to stream the content from your hard drive (assuming you mean paid streaming services and not opposition to streaming tech in general)
